arjun: Heads up — while patching base images for the recent OpenSSL/glibc CVE chain (CVE-2026-1420) I hit runtime failures in a few services after switching to alpine:3.19 + openssl 3.1.5. Repro steps and stack:
```
ImportError: /lib/libcrypto.so.3: undefined symbol: SSLv23_method
  at _cffi_backend.c: ...
  service logs: embeddings-worker crashed on import cryptography.hazmat.bindings
```
This looks like a symbol/versioning compatibility break: some wheels/native extensions expect the old symbol names (libcrypto.so.1.1). I can reproduce locally by running the wheel in the new image.
maya: Which services are affected and how wide is the blast radius? Can we canary? :thinking:
arjun: Affected: ingress-proxy (rust binding to openssl), embeddings-worker (python wheel using cffi), spark-transformer (java JNI). Traffic impact limited to internal batch workers so low risk for initial canary. I propose a minimal compat image for canary.
liam: Options:
- Backport libssl 1.1 into the image (safe but larger surface and maintenance)
- Add a compat shim layer with symlinks: provide `libcrypto.so.1.1 -> libcrypto.so.3`
- Rebuild native wheels against openssl 3.x (longer work)
Symlink approach is fastest for canary but could mask ABI differences.
sophia: Security note: upstream OpenSSL guidance warns that symlinking across major versions is not a true compatibility fix and may change behavior. For CVE-2026-1420 vendor recommends rebuilds where possible. Use symlink only as temporary mitigation with tight canary windows and monitoring.
arjun: Proposed canary plan (draft):
1) Build `redwood/base:alpine-crypto-compat-2026-01` that layers a small compat package with ldconfig + crafted symlinks for `libcrypto.so.1.1`/`libssl.so.1.1` -> `libcrypto.so.3`/`libssl.so.3` and sets `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` appropriately.
2) Smoke tests: import cryptography + run small native unit test, run ingress-proxy integration smoke, run embeddings inference sample.
3) Canary rollout to `staging-low` (1 replica per zone) for 24h with 1m checks — rollback on any 5xx >0.5% or import failures.
4) If stable → schedule progressive rollout + plan to rebuild wheels and/or backport packages.
Dockerfile snippet for compat layer:
```
FROM alpine:3.19
RUN apk add --no-cache openssl=3.1.5-r0
# compat shim
RUN mkdir -p /usr/lib/compat && \
    ln -s /usr/lib/libcrypto.so.3 /usr/lib/compat/libcrypto.so.1.1 && \
    ln -s /usr/lib/libssl.so.3 /usr/lib/compat/libssl.so.1.1 && \
    echo "/usr/lib/compat" > /etc/ld.so.conf.d/compat.conf && ldconfig
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/compat:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
```
jen: If we build a new image we need to re-sign it and update attestations. Will this require KMS key rotation? Also we need permission to push the compat image from the CI identity.
deploy-bot: New image pushed to staging-canary: sha256:abcd1234compat (timestamp: 1841234610). Deploy job started for namespace `staging-low`.
arjun: We'll re-sign with the same KMS key (no rotation), but we must add an audit entry and bump the SBOM. Action: I'll file the image-sign PR and trigger re-sign. Also need a short-lived registry push role for `ci-builder` — suggest 2h window and then revoke.
liam: Add regression checks for python deps before canary: inside the image run:
```
python -m venv /tmp/v && /tmp/v/bin/pip install wheel cryptography
/tmp/v/bin/python -c "import cryptography.hazmat.bindings.openssl; print('ok')"
```
Also test JNI loading for spark-transformer: `java -Djava.library.path=/usr/lib/compat -jar smoke.jar`.
maya: Sounds good. Proposed schedule: canary deploy tonight 23:30 UTC, monitor for 24h. I'll own the monitoring dashboard and will watch for 5xx, OOM, and import errors. :thumbsup:
sophia: Compliance: capture audit logs for who pushed and who deployed the compat image. Ensure SBOM is attached and note that this is a temporary mitigation in the vuln tracker: https://internal/redwood/vuln-triage/entries/1841234567 (I'll file).
arjun: Action items summarized:
- arjun: build compat image + PR for image-sign and SBOM (in progress)
- jen: open temporary registry push window for `ci-builder` and coord with infra (ETA: +30m)
- maya: start canary 23:30 UTC + monitor dashboard (24h)
- liam: add wheel/JNI smoke tests to canary pipeline (PR welcome)
- sophia: update vuln tracker entry and compliance notes

If canary shows any of: import errors, >0.5% 5xx, OOM spikes → immediate rollback and we start the backport/rebuild plan. Otherwise we'll use canary data to prioritize rebuilding wheels vs maintaining a backport package.
Thanks — posting updates here as we go.
